name: The Offspring
label: Epitaph
lede: A $20,000 record, a janitor's day job and one KROQ DJ's hunch made Smash the best-selling independent-label album ever, and then the band left the label that made it.

eras.title: Garage kids from Cypress
eras.text: Two friends, a Social Distortion riot and a drummer who wanted to be a doctor: the band that would sell millions began as a Southern California club act with a self-run label and a debut nobody heard.

years.h: Dexter Holland and Greg K. start playing in a garage
years.p: Bryan "Dexter" Holland and Greg Kriesel began playing together in Cypress, California in 1983. After a riot at a Social Distortion show in 1984 they formed Manic Subsidal with drummer James Lilja.

years.h: Noodles joins from Clowns of Death
years.p: Guitarist Kevin "Noodles" Wasserman, of the band Clowns of Death, was recruited into Manic Subsidal. The first show was in Santa Cruz, opening for White Flag and Scared Straight.

years.h: Manic Subsidal becomes The Offspring
years.p: The band renamed itself and put out its first single, "I'll Be Waiting", on its own Black Label imprint. A demo tape that year got a good notice in Maximum Rocknroll.

years.h: Ron Welty replaces Lilja at 16
years.p: Drummer James Lilja left in 1987 to pursue a medical career in oncology. Sixteen-year-old Ron Welty took over the kit.

years.h: Debut album on Nemesis, vinyl and cassette only
years.p: Recorded with producer Thom Wilson in summer 1989 and put out by Nemesis Records. The CD did not arrive until 1995.

eras.title: Baghdad, Epitaph and Ignition
eras.text: A 7-inch made with Thom Wilson opened the door at Brett Gurewitz's Epitaph, and the band began to build a following on tours with Pennywise, Lunachicks and NOFX.

years.h: The Baghdad 7-inch gets them signed to Epitaph
years.p: The Baghdad EP, made with producer Thom Wilson, led to the band signing with [[Brett Gurewitz|cd40188b-ea30-4729-bebb-e8c5091c9d02]]'s Epitaph Records.

years.h: Ignition, the first Epitaph album
years.p: The band toured it across the U.S. with [[Pennywise|5c210861-2ce2-4be3-9307-bbcfc361cc01]] and Lunachicks, then in Europe with [[NOFX|dcaa4f81-bfb7-44eb-8594-4e74f004b6e4]]. It was a proper club-circuit punk record, and it was the last one before everything changed.

eras.title: Smash
eras.text: A $20,000 record, a janitor's day job and one radio DJ's pick turned a small Epitaph band into the label's whole story. Smash went on to be called the best-selling independent-label album ever.

years.cap: The Offspring. A good set, but they were completely overshadowed by Greenday. · Wikimedia
years.h: Smash is cut in 20 days at Track Record Studios
years.p: Producer Thom Wilson recorded it in North Hollywood on a budget of about $20,000, and the band took discounted studio time when it opened up.
years.xp: Wilson, who had worked with the band from the first record, lived in a camper van during the sessions, according to a Louder feature. The band's day jobs were still the real ones: Noodles was a janitor at Earl Warren Middle School near Disneyland and Greg K. worked at a print shop, while Dexter Holland studied at USC.

years.h: Smash out April 8 on Epitaph
years.p: The third album came out with a skeleton on the cover and a lead single, "Come Out and Play", inspired by Holland's drives through gang-hit parts of South L.A.

years.h: KROQ's Jed the Fish makes "Come Out and Play" a hit
years.p: According to Rolling Stone, DJ Jed the Fish picked the song as his "Catch of the Day" at KROQ, and heavy rotation followed. It topped Billboard's Modern Rock chart, and Noodles quit his janitor job that summer.
years.xp:
The video was shot for about $5,000 in a friend's garage, with much of the money going to barbecue for the extras, per Louder. The album went gold and platinum within about four months, according to Wikipedia.

"Self Esteem" and "Gotta Get Away" followed as singles.

years.h: Holland and Greg K. start Nitro Records
years.p: The pair launched Nitro and re-released the 1989 debut. The label went on to sign [[The Vandals|f54fc7c3-3a40-4f26-83cf-328d9b097e93]], Guttermouth, Jughead's Revenge and [[AFI|1c3919b2-43ca-4a4a-935d-9d50135ec0ef]].

years.h: From opening act to arenas
years.p: Tours with Weezer, [[Quicksand|3c9f8bef-a658-4204-9ee8-7e95d2535b32]] and No Use for a Name, plus Japan and Australia's Big Day Out, moved the band from clubs to theaters and arenas, according to Wikipedia.

eras.title: The Epitaph split
eras.text: A record that made an independent label rich set up a contract fight. The band left for Columbia, and some punk fans never forgave it.

years.cap: The Offspring performing lite in Fortaleza, Brazil, November 15th 2008 · Wikimedia
years.h: The Offspring leave Epitaph for Columbia
years.p: Their lawyer cited "fundamental reasons" and said Epitaph had breached the contract. Epitaph still held the back catalog, and reissued remastered Ignition and Smash in 2008.

years.big: The band thought Smash's money deserved better terms
q: I never wanted to sell the Offspring to a major label.
years.h: Two years of haggling over Smash money
years.p: Epitaph's owner said he never wanted to sell The Offspring to a major label.
years.xp: Rolling Stone reported the band felt its outsized contribution to Epitaph's revenue justified better terms. Gurewitz said he was heartbroken at the loss.

years.h: Ixnay on the Hombre, the first Columbia album
years.p: It sold well but not "Smash Part Two", as Holland acknowledged fans expected. Holland directed the video for "I Choose" himself.

eras.title: Pretty Fly and the Napster summer
eras.text: Americana made them a global pop act. The next record became a fight with their own label over free downloads.

years.h: Americana: "Pretty Fly" tops charts in nine countries
years.p: Three singles, including "Why Don't You Get a Job?" and "The Kids Aren't Alright", ruled radio and MTV. Wikipedia lists the album as peaking at number two in the U.S.

years.cap: The Offspring during Rock am Ring at Nürburgring, Nürburg, Rheinland-Pfalz, G... · Wikimedia
years.h: Weird Al turns "Pretty Fly" into "Pretty Fly for a Rabbi"
years.p: [[Weird Al Yankovic|7746d775-9550-4360-b8d5-c37bd448ce01]] parodied the song. It's the surest sign a band has arrived.

years.h: Idle Hands and Woodstock '99
years.p: The band played "I Wanna Be Sedated" and "Beheaded" in the movie Idle Hands, and appeared at Woodstock '99.

years.h: Conspiracy of One and the free download that wasn't
years.p: The band wanted to release the whole album online. Sony threatened legal action, so only "Original Prankster" went on the site, and the rest leaked to fan sites.
years.xp: The band sold Napster-branded T-shirts and gave the profits to Napster creator Shawn Fanning, per Wikipedia. The album still went platinum.

years.h: Ron Welty is out after 16 years
years.p: Welty said he left to join Steady Ground. Later reports said Holland and Noodles fired him without notice before the seventh album.
years.xp: Josh Freese drummed on the Splinter sessions and Atom Willard, ex-Rocket from the Crypt, joined for touring. Welty sued in 2020 over royalties from the $35 million catalog sale and lost in March 2023, when the judge called some of his claims "completely illogical."

years.h: Splinter, with electronic samples on "Hit That"
years.p: The seventh album and the last of the original Columbia deal, with Freese on drums.

eras.title: Warped Tour, a PhD and a $35 million sale
eras.text: The band settled into a long stadium-and-festival career, and its leader finished a doctorate.

years.h: First Vans Warped Tour
years.p: The summer 2005 run followed the Greatest Hits collection. Drummer Atom Willard later joined Angels & Airwaves.

years.h: Rise and Fall, Rage and Grace
years.p: With producer Bob Rock, the single "You're Gonna Go Far, Kid" spent 11 weeks at the top of Hot Modern Rock Tracks, a record for the band.
play: Rise and Fall, Rage and Grace

years.h: Days Go By
years.p: Made with Bob Rock in Hawaii after sessions began in 2010.

years.h: Summer Nationals: Smash at 20
years.p: A co-headline tour with [[Bad Religion|149e6720-4e4a-41a4-afca-6d29083fc091]], Pennywise, [[The Vandals|f54fc7c3-3a40-4f26-83cf-328d9b097e93]], Stiff Little Fingers and [[Naked Raygun|85d2e30c-92fd-4c7f-a2dc-f988a70e234d]] celebrated Smash's 20th anniversary.

years.h: Round Hill buys the catalog for $35 million
years.p: The band had reclaimed its Columbia albums in 2014 and auctioned them from 2015. Round Hill Music paid $35 million for the catalog and publishing.

years.h: Dexter Holland earns a PhD in molecular biology
years.p: Holland finished the doctorate at USC.

eras.title: Bassist out, lawsuits, new drummer
eras.text: Long-serving members left in the courtroom, but the band kept touring and kept making records.

years.cap: The Offspring at Rock Allegiance 2016. · Wikimedia
years.h: Greg K. is out of the band he co-founded
years.p: Holland and Noodles told him he could no longer play or record with the band. Tony Kanal of No Doubt filled in for tours, and Todd Morse became the full-time bassist.
years.xp: Kriesel sued in August 2019. Holland and Noodles countersued, saying he was asked and agreed to leave and that they tried to buy out his share. The case settled out of court in 2023, per Wikipedia.

years.h: Let the Bad Times Roll, first album on Concord
years.p: Released April 16 after a February announcement.

years.h: Pete Parada leaves the drummer's seat
years.p: Parada said he was fired after declining a COVID-19 vaccine on his doctor's advice. Holland and Noodles said in November 2021 that they hired replacements for crew safety.

years.cap: The Offspring performing at Stockwell in London, 29th August 2009 · Wikimedia
years.h: Original drummer James Lilja plays "Beheaded" after 36 years
years.p: Lilja, who co-wrote the song, sat in on August 6, 2023. Brandon Pertzborn had joined as permanent drummer in May.

years.h: Brandon Pertzborn takes the drums
years.p: Josh Freese left to replace the late Taylor Hawkins in Foo Fighters. Pertzborn, formerly of Black Flag and Suicidal Tendencies, joined.

years.h: Supercharged, the eleventh album
years.p: Released October 11 on Concord after the June single "Make It All Right".

sources.title: Rolling Stone: Smash, the little punk LP that defeated the majors
